slides.teacher_cue: Three new spellings today. ph = /f/: phone, photo, graph, phrase. Another spelling of the /f/ sound you know. gh = /f/ (in certain positions): enough, rough, tough, laugh. The gh is silent in many words but makes /f/ in these. -igh = /aɪ/: high, night, light, right, bright, flight, knight. The gh is silent — -igh = long /aɪ/ + silent gh. Group 8 is complete after this lesson.
slides.expected_response: Students read ph, gh/f, and -igh words correctly using the new spelling-sound correspondences.
slides.correction_move: Establish each pattern. ph = /f/: same sound as f, different spelling (Greek origin). gh = /f/: only in specific words — enough, rough, tough. -igh = /aɪ/: the igh is a unit, gh is silent, i is long.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students attempting to blend g+h separately in -igh and gh words.

slides.expected_response: Students say phone orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model phone orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for ph = /f/ — same sound as f.

slides.teacher_cue: Say photo — a picture. ph = /f/, two open syllables. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say photo orally and connect meaning before blending.

slides.observation_note: Watch for ph = /f/ and long /oʊ/ in both syllables.

slides.teacher_cue: Say enough — sufficient. gh = /f/ here. en + ough. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say enough orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model enough orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for gh = /f/ at the end — unusual but important.

slides.teacher_cue: Say night — darkness. -igh = /aɪ/, gh is silent. Reveal and blend.

slides.observation_note: Watch for -igh = long /aɪ/ — not /ɪg/ or /ɪh/.

slides.teacher_cue: Say flight — the act of flying. fl cluster + -igh = /aɪ/. Reveal and blend.
